D000375.s: The gradual irreversible changes in structure and function of an organism that occur as a result of the passage of time.

D000726.s: Compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or actions of androgens.

D000753.s: A severe sometimes chronic anemia, usually macrocytic in type, that does not respond to ordinary antianemic therapy.

D001017.s: A birth defect characterized by the narrowing of the aorta that can be of varying degree and at any point from the transverse arch to the iliac bifurcation. Aortic coarctation causes arterial hypertension before the point of narrowing and arterial hypotension beyond the narrowed portion.

D001291.s: Attitudes of personnel toward their patients, other professionals, toward the medical care system, etc.

D001422.s: Physicochemical property of fimbriated (fimbriae, bacterial) and non-fimbriated bacteria of attaching to cells, tissue, and nonbiological surfaces. It is a factor in bacterial colonization and pathogenicity.

D001686.s: Biological processes, properties, and characteristics of the whole organism in human, animal, microorganisms, and plants, and of the biosphere.

D001718.s: The property of nonisotropic media, such as crystals, whereby a single incident beam of light traverses the medium as two beams, each plane-polarized, the planes being at right angles to each other. (Cline et al., Dictionary of Visual Science, 4th ed)

D003107.s: A surgical specialty concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of disorders and abnormalities of the colon; rectum; and anal canal.

D003864.s: The decrease in a measurable parameter of a physiological process, including cellular, microbial, and plant; immunological, cardiovascular, respiratory, reproductive, urinary, digestive, neural, musculoskeletal, ocular, and skin physiological processes; or metabolic process, including enzymatic and…

D004407.s: A malignant ovarian neoplasm, thought to be derived from primordial germ cells of the sexually undifferentiated embryonic gonad. It is the counterpart of the classical seminoma of the testis, to which it is both grossly and histologically identical.

D004793.s: Compounds which restore enzymatic activity by removing an inhibitory group bound to the reactive site of the enzyme.

D004832.s: A seizure disorder usually occurring in childhood characterized by rhythmic electrical brain discharges of generalized onset. Clinical features include a sudden cessation of ongoing activity usually without loss of postural tone.

D006045.s: An enlarged thyroid gland with at least 50% of the gland situated behind the sternum. It is an unusual presentation of an intrathoracic goiter. Substernal goiters frequently cause compression on the trachea leading to deviation, narrowing, and respiratory symptoms.

D006399.s: A blood-filled vagina that is obstructed.

D007002.s: The 12th cranial nerve. The hypoglossal nerve originates in the hypoglossal nucleus of the medulla and supplies motor innervation to all of the muscles of the tongue except the palatoglossus (which is supplied by the vagus). This nerve also contains proprioceptive afferents from the tongue muscles.

D007244.s: A common, acute infection usually caused by the Epstein-Barr virus (herpesvirus 4, human). There is an increase in mononuclear white blood cells and other atypical lymphocytes, generalized lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and occasionally hepatomegaly with hepatitis.

D007587.s: Statement of the position requirements, qualifications for the position, wage range, and any special conditions expected of the employee.

D007613.s: Nonsusceptibility of bacteria to the antibiotic kanamycin, which can bind to their 70S ribosomes and cause misreading of messenger RNA.

D007738.s: Deformities of the spine characterized by an exaggerated convexity of the vertebral column. The forward bending of the thoracic region usually is more than 40 degrees. This deformity sometimes is called round back or hunchback.

D007914.s: Residential treatment centers for individuals with leprosy.

D008018.s: The continuous sequence of changes undergone by living organisms during the post-embryonic developmental process, such as metamorphosis in insects and amphibians. This includes the developmental stages of apicomplexans such as the malarial parasite, plasmodium falciparum.

D008186.s: Chemical compounds that cause luteolysis or degeneration of the corpus luteum.

D008591.s: Congenital, or rarely acquired, herniation of meningeal and spinal cord tissue through a bony defect in the vertebral column. The majority of these defects occur in the lumbosacral region. Clinical features include paraplegia, loss of sensation in the lower body, and incontinence.

D009347.s: A syndrome characterized by hyperpigmentation, enlarging pituitary mass, visual defects secondary to compression of the optic chiasm, and elevated serum ACTH.

D009541.s: A fold of the mucous membrane of the conjunctiva in many animals. At rest, it is hidden in the medial canthus. It can extend to cover part or all of the cornea to help clean the cornea.

D010190.s: Tumors or cancer of the pancreas. Depending on the types of islet cells present in the tumors, various hormones can be secreted: glucagon from pancreatic alpha cells; insulin from pancreatic beta cells; and somatostatin from the somatostatin-secreting cells.

D010482.s: Acute or chronic inflammation of tissues surrounding the apical portion of a tooth, associated with the collection of pus, resulting from infection following pulp infection through a carious lesion or as a result of an injury causing pulp necrosis. (Dorland, 27th ed)

D010565.s: A mode of communication concerned with inducing or urging the adoption of certain beliefs, theories, or lines of action by others.

D011603.s: The study of the physiological basis of human and animal behavior.

D012167.s: Perforations through the whole thickness of the retina including the macula as the result of inflammation, trauma, degeneration, etc. The concept includes retinal breaks, tears, dialyses, and holes.

D012448.s: A condition in which there is a derivation of pleasure from inflicting pain, discomfort or humiliation on another person or persons. The sexual significance of sadistic wishes or behavior may be conscious or unconscious.

D012637.s: Regulations to assure protection of property and equipment.

D013494.s: A degenerative disease of the central nervous system characterized by balance difficulties; ocular motility disorders (supranuclear ophthalmoplegia); dysarthria; swallowing difficulties; and axial dystonia. Onset is usually in the fifth decade and disease progression occurs over several years.

D013779.s: An aminoperhydroquinazoline poison found mainly in the liver and ovaries of fishes in the order tetraodontiformes, which are eaten. The toxin causes paresthesia and paralysis through interference with neuromuscular conduction.

D014855.s: Degeneration of distal aspects of a nerve axon following injury to the cell body or proximal portion of the axon. The process is characterized by fragmentation of the axon and its myelin sheath.

D015625.s: Devices used to generate extra soft tissue in vivo to be used in surgical reconstructions. They exert stretching forces on the tissue and thus stimulate new growth and result in tissue expansion.

D016750.s: A condition characterized by persistent spasms (spasm) involving multiple muscles, primarily in the lower limbs and trunk. The illness tends to occur in the fourth to sixth decade of life, presenting with intermittent spasms that become continuous.

D017065.s: Work consisting of a set of directions or principles to assist the health care practitioner with patient care decisions about appropriate diagnostic, therapeutic, or other clinical procedures for specific clinical circumstances.

D017490.s: A chronic, congenital ichthyosis inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. Infants are usually born encased in a collodion membrane which sheds within a few weeks. Scaling is generalized and marked with grayish-brown quadrilateral scales, adherent at their centers and free at the edges.

D018600.s: A branch of embryology for the study of congenital malformations and developmental abnormalities.

D018709.s: A class of statistical methods applicable to a large set of probability distributions used to test for correlation, location, independence, etc. In most nonparametric statistical tests, the original scores or observations are replaced by another variable containing less information.

D019140.s: The giving of attention to the special dental needs of children, including the prevention of tooth diseases and instruction in dental hygiene and dental health. The dental care may include the services provided by dental specialists.

D020298.s: A human cell line established from a diffuse histiocytic lymphoma (histiocytic lymphoma, diffuse) and displaying many monocytic characteristics. It serves as an in vitro model for monocyte and macrophage differentiation.

D020306.s: Tuberculosis of the brain, spinal cord, or meninges (tuberculosis, meningeal), most often caused by mycobacterium tuberculosis and rarely by mycobacterium bovis. The infection may be limited to the nervous system or coexist in other organs (e.g., tuberculosis, pulmonary).

D020423.s: Disease involving the median nerve, from its origin at the brachial plexus to its termination in the hand.

D027602.s: A DNA sequence that is found in the promoter region of many growth-related genes. The regulatory transcription factor serum response factor binds to and regulates the activity of genes containing this element.

D045743.s: A rapid onset form of systemic scleroderma with progressive widespread SKIN thickening over the arms, the legs and the trunk, resulting in stiffness and disability.

D047468.s: The aggregation of soluble antigens with antibodies, alone or with antibody binding factors such as ANTI-antibodies or staphylococcal protein A, into complexes large enough to fall out of solution.

D049471.s: The stage in the first meiotic prophase, following zygotene stage, when crossing over between homologous chromosomes begins.

D053058.s: Cells or feeding stage in the life cycle of sporozoan protozoa. In the malarial parasite, the trophozoite develops from the merozoite and then splits into the schizont. Trophozoites that are left over from cell division can go on to form gametocytes.

D053627.s: A condition in which the percentage of motile sperm is abnormally low.

D054327.s: Compounds that provide lubrication between surfaces in order to reduce friction.

D056769.s: Rare autosomal recessive disease characterized by multiple organ dysfunction. The key clinical features include retinal degeneration (nystagmus, pathologic; retinitis pigmentosa; and eventual blindness), childhood obesity, sensorineural hearing loss, and normal mental development.

D056989.s: Myocardial infarction in which the inferior wall of the heart is involved. It is often caused by occlusion of the right coronary artery.

D062065.s: Contaminated water generated as a waste product of human activity.

D000070604.s: Congenital, complete or partial fusion of the tarsal bones of the foot. Pes planus is usually a feature.

D000076282.s: A process of waste disposal involving the conversion of green waste (i.e. leaves, organic matter, food waste, manure) into soil-enhancing matter.

D000080445.n: Asthma-Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Overlap Syndrome
D000080445.s: Syndrome with clinical features of both asthma and COPD.

D000084522.s: A specialized subpopulation of CD4+ T cells involved in formation of germinal center. Tfh cells are mostly located in secondary lymphoid organs, e.g., tonsil; spleen and lymph nodes.

D000091003.s: This encompasses a number of challenges, such as having trouble paying rent, living in overcrowded conditions, moving frequently, living with friends or relatives out of necessity, being unhoused, or spending the bulk of household income (>50%) on housing.

D000091542.s: Characteristics that may describe the demographic, social, built environment, or economic characteristics of a geographic area in which people live and can affect health and well-being of neighborhood residents.

D000092525.s: Coronal plane fractures of the femur condyle at the KNEE.

D000096042.s: The subjective, quantifiable prevalence, frequency, and severity of symptoms placing a physiologic burden on patients and producing multiple negative, physical, and emotional patient responses.

D000097913.s: Contrast imaging generated from the measurements of phase shift changes of light waves as they pass through transparent objects of varying thickness and refractivity.
